free_tier.stated: Storage explicitly unlimited ('Upload whatever size you want'); no per-file cap; no bandwidth cap. Free files start with an 8-day life, +2 days per download up to 60d, and become permanent at 30+ downloads every 60 days (live pricing page, 2026-08-24 capture; the 2026-10 live page is 404 to non-browser fetchers).

retention.stated: Free files start with an 8-day life, +2 days per download up to 60d, and become permanent at 30+ downloads every 60 days (live pricing page, 2026-08-24 capture; the 2026-10 live page is 404 to non-browser fetchers)

egress.terms: Unmetered. Help page: 'Bandwidth Limits? None. Go wild.' Downloads are served through Cloudflare with a Turnstile/hx gate but no transfer meter. Hotlinking historically allowed per 2024 FAQ.

tooling: PUT upload to https://w.buzzheavier.com/{name} (anonymous) or /{parentId}/{name} with 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCOUNT_ID>'. Bash CLI github.com/Ognisty321/buzzheavier-cli; uploader modules in anasty17/mirror-leech-telegram-bot (PR #1938/#1939) and SilentDemonSD/WZML-X (PR #418); download resolver in towerwatchman/Atlas electron/downloads/hosts/buzzheavier.js.
chaining: Anonymous PUT needs no account at all, so the ceiling is not per-account: it is 'as many files as you can push'. Account IDs are free, non-recoverable, email-less, and unlimited. The 45-day inactivity expiry resets when the same client re-downloads its own file (>10% or the download endpoint), and the same bytes may sit under 2-3 identifiers. Docs also expose ?expiry= and ?burner= for self-expiring uploads.
limits_note: No per-file cap (docs: 'name max 500 chars' is the only field limit). Upload rate: 2 req/s and 10 concurrent uploads per IP observed on FileDitch-class peers; Buzzheavier returned no rate headers in probes. Download path is Cloudflare-Turnstile gated: a plain curl GET of a file page returns 403 'Just a moment', and /{id}/download?t=... returns HTTP 204 + 'Hx-Redirect' back to the file page unless the browser completes the human-verification step. Retention: 8d base / +2d per download / 60d cap / permanent at 30 downloads per 60 days; older policy was 15d/+3d/45d/15 downloads.

identity_cost.detail: derived from the record's prose, not from an identity field, and no signup was executed: wn blog admits the cheap storage was storage resold below cost at ~$1/TB/month, which collapsed after a seizure at the upstream provider and a provider crackdown; they now pay ~EUR 5-6/TB/month.
